test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 17 Oct, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Study the following graph carefully and answer the question given below it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f2f1592468c73a6301332bec0b6ceec903c245a8c58c1e169f897dece85cb9e3.png] 

In which of the following years was the percentage increase in production from the previous year the ma×imum among the given years?
solution:
**Formula Used:**

Percentage increase = [(Current year production - Previous year production) / Previous year production] × 100

**Calculation:**

For 1990: Percentage increase = [(40 - 25) / 25] × 100 = (15 / 25) × 100 = 0.6 × 100 = 60%

For 1991: Percentage increase = [(60 - 40) / 40] × 100 = (20 / 40) × 100 = 0.5 × 100 = 50%

For 1992: Percentage increase = [(45 - 60) / 60] × 100 = (-15 / 60) × 100 = -0.25 × 100 = -25% (decrease)

For 1993: Percentage increase = [(65 - 45) / 45] × 100 = (20 / 45) × 100 ≈ 0.4444 × 100 ≈ 44.44%

For 1994: Percentage increase = [(50 - 65) / 65] × 100 = (-15 / 65) × 100 ≈ -0.2308 × 100 ≈ -23.08% (decrease)

For 1995: Percentage increase = [(75 - 50) / 50] × 100 = (25 / 50) × 100 = 0.5 × 100 = 50%

For 1996: Percentage increase = [(80 - 75) / 75] × 100 = (5 / 75) × 100 ≈ 0.0667 × 100 ≈ 6.67%

Comparing the percentage increases:

1990: 60%

1991: 50%

1993: ≈ 44.44%

1995: 50%

1996: ≈ 6.67%

**The percentage increase in production from the previous year was the ma×imum in 1990.**
